subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Sustained development of a personal project

questions.q: Component 3 (Coursework) requires candidates to produce work that shows the sustained development of what?
options: A personal project developed over time
A written essay on art history
An exact copy of a famous painting
questions.explain: Coursework is centred on the sustained development of a candidate's own personal project.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an art medium?
questions.explain: Charcoal is a physical medium, whereas composition, balance and contrast are visual concepts.

questions.q: Which of the following is a printmaking process?
questions.explain: Lino printing is a printmaking process, while the others are drawing techniques for creating tone.

questions.q: Working directly from an object, person or place that is physically present provides what kind of source material?
questions.explain: First-hand observation of a subject that is physically present provides primary source material.

questions.q: Gathering images from books, magazines or the internet provides what kind of source material?
questions.explain: Material collected from existing images rather than direct observation is secondary source material.

questions.q: In coursework, a 'personal project' is best described as which of the following?
options: A self-directed body of work developed around a chosen starting point or theme
A set of unrelated technical exercises
A timed test completed in one sitting
A reproduction of the teacher's demonstration piece
questions.explain: A personal project is a coherent, self-directed body of work built around the candidate's own theme.

questions.q: Which of the following would be classified as a three-dimensional process?
questions.explain: Clay modelling produces three-dimensional form, while the others are two-dimensional processes.

questions.q: Why do candidates annotate their sketchbook work?
options: To explain their thinking, evaluate outcomes and show the reasoning behind decisions
To fill empty space on the page
To increase the word count of the project
To replace the need for any drawings
questions.explain: Annotation makes a candidate's thinking, evaluation and decision-making visible to the assessor.

questions.q: Experimenting with a range of media and techniques mainly allows a candidate to do what?
options: Discover which methods best communicate their ideas
Avoid learning any single technique properly
Prove that they own many materials
questions.explain: Trialling different media helps candidates find the most effective means of expressing their ideas.

questions.q: 'Sustained development' in a personal project is best evidenced by which of the following?
options: A logical progression of ideas from starting point through experimentation to resolution
A single finished piece with no preparatory work
Many unrelated drawings with no connecting theme
An exact copy of one artist's work
questions.explain: Sustained development shows ideas evolving coherently from starting point to a resolved outcome.

questions.q: Why is drawing from primary sources generally valued more highly than working only from photographs?
options: It records first-hand observation, giving a more personal and informed understanding of the subject
It is always quicker to do
It removes the need to refine ideas
questions.explain: First-hand observation gives a fuller, more personal understanding than working from photographs alone.

questions.q: The main purpose of producing media 'trials' or samples is to do what?
options: Test the qualities and effects of materials before committing to a final outcome
Show the teacher every material available
questions.explain: Media trials let candidates explore the effects of materials before deciding on a final piece.

questions.q: How does researching relevant artists support a personal project?
options: It provides ideas and approaches the candidate can respond to and adapt in their own work
It allows the candidate to copy an artwork and submit it as their own
It replaces the need to develop personal ideas
It is only used to fill a bibliography
questions.explain: Artist research offers approaches candidates can respond to and adapt, informing their own development.

questions.q: 'Refining ideas' during a project involves which of the following?
options: Selecting, editing and improving ideas based on evaluation of earlier work
Starting a completely new project each week
questions.explain: Refining means evaluating earlier work and selectively editing and improving ideas.

questions.q: A candidate wants to capture the delicate, translucent quality of flower petals. Which medium would be most appropriate to trial first?
questions.explain: Watercolour's translucency is well suited to conveying the delicate, light-filled quality of petals.

questions.q: A candidate's sketchbook contains only downloaded photographs and no drawings. What is the most useful advice to strengthen their recording?
options: Produce first-hand observational studies from primary sources
Move straight to the final piece
questions.explain: Adding first-hand observational studies strengthens recording by introducing primary source evidence.

questions.q: A student has one strong final painting but almost no preparatory work. To meet the requirements of coursework, they should do what?
options: Provide evidence of the development that led to the piece, including studies and experiments
questions.explain: Coursework must show the sustained development, so supporting studies and experiments are required.

questions.q: A candidate exploring the theme 'decay' wants to combine torn paper, photographs and paint on a single surface. Which process are they using?
questions.explain: Combining several different materials on one surface is a mixed media collage process.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Art & Design (0400) syllabus; Component 3: Coursework
